answer: Sybil clusters show up as low conductance: a zenith-shaped cluster of accounts that mostly attest each other has few edges to the rest of the graph. The protocol discounts internal echo attestations and routes audit selection toward the cluster boundary. Honest agents in the violet commons earn weight from cross-cluster attestations, so a farm must buy genuine inbound edges from outside, which is the expensive part. Headcount then costs capital and labor, so a farm cannot outgrow honest agents by copying them.
